OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's postcode. Optional; when present it must be a 4-digit value
            and, when the city has a known region (Sydney -> NSW, Melbourne -> VIC,
            Brisbane -> QLD), must fall within that region's inclusive range (NSW 2000-2099,
            VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit
            postcode. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized
            to E.164 form; a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: The owner's date of birth. Optional on create; when present it is used to
            derive the owner's ageBand relative to the registrationDate. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true on create, bypasses the household duplicate block so this owner
            can be registered even though another owner already shares its household (the same last
            name, compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace, and postcode). Such an
            owner is created as a declared household member and is not flagged as a possible
            duplicate. Otherwise a create sharing an existing household is rejected with 409
            Conflict. Request-only; not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0

content.text:
Now I have a clear picture. Key findings:

- Tests run under `hsqldb` + `ddl-auto=none`, so the schema comes from `schema.sql` with no Hibernate schema management. Adding `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` columns to the `Owner` entity now would emit SQL against non-existent columns and break every owner test — that's part of *implementing* the change (new storage/contract), not restructuring. So I must not add those fields yet.
- The genuinely-safe, behavior-preserving preparation is in the controller: the address step is currently inlined inside `normalizeAndValidateFields`, unlike every other concern (email, postcode, telephone) which has its own helper. Extracting a `normalizeAddressFields(Owner)` helper creates the exact single seam the future change needs — where structured-field selection, per-field normalization, and composition into the stored `address` will live — which is also what keeps the future `Owner` accessors thin (composition stays in the controller, not the model getters).

Let me make that extraction.

content.text:
The full test suite is exactly these two acceptance tests. State before my change: `functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress` green, `coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress` red (the acceptance test for the upcoming feature itself). State after: identical — no regressions, all currently-passing tests still green.

## What I did

I prepared `OwnerRestControllerV1` so the structured-address change can land as a localized, idiomatic edit rather than swelling code in the wrong places.

**The one behavior-preserving restructuring:** extracted the address step out of `normalizeAndValidateFields` into a dedicated `normalizeAddressFields(Owner)` helper.

Before, address handling was the odd one out — inlined directly in the orchestrator:
```java
String address = normalizeAddress(owner.getAddress());
if (address.isEmpty()) return false;
owner.setAddress(address);
```
while every other concern (email, postcode via `isPostcodeValidForCity`, telephone via `normalizeTelephone`) already had its own helper. Now `normalizeAndValidateFields` is a uniform sequence of per-concern steps, and there's a single seam — `normalizeAddressFields` — that reads the address input, canonicalizes it, and writes back the stored `address`. That is exactly where the upcoming change belongs: structured-field selection (`addressLine1`/`addressLine2` preferred, flat `address` as fallback), per-field normalization, and composing the returned `address` string all fit inside that one method, next to the existing `normalizeAddress` token-normalizer.

## Why I deliberately did *not* touch `Owner`

The hotspot list names future `Owner.getAddressLine1/setAddressLine1/getAddressLine2/setAddressLine2` accessors, but I confirmed those cannot be added now without *implementing* the change:

- Tests run under the `hsqldb` profile with `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none`, so the schema is fixed by `schema.sql`. Adding `@Column`-mapped `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` fields would emit SQL against non-existent columns and break every owner create/read — a storage/contract change, not a restructuring.

The right preparation for those accessors is indirect: by giving address normalization and composition a clear home in the controller (`normalizeAddressFields`), the maintainer implementing the feature will keep the future `Owner` accessors as plain field getters/setters, instead of leaking normalization/composition into the model — which is what made them "carry more complexity than they can hold" in the direct implementation.

The change itself remains unimplemented, as instructed; its acceptance test (`coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress`) stays red exactly as it was before.
